page: Amazon Web Services r7a.32xlarge is an enterprise-scale memory-optimized virtual machine driven by dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Architected on the x86_64 platform using the AWS Nitro System, it delivers 128 physical cores across 128 vCPUs with a single thread per core, eliminating hyper-threading concurrency penalties and operating at frequencies up to 3.7 GHz. The system provides 1024 GB of high-speed DDR5 system memory running at 5 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio (8 GB per core). Network connectivity is provisioned at a baseline rate of 50 Gbps. Notably, the instance features no bundled local NVMe storage and contains no hardware GPU accelerators, directing primary storage workflows entirely through network-attached block devices.

Benchmark evaluations show top-tier execution across parallel computing and memory-bound tasks. The server demonstrates exceptional multi-core throughput in stress-ng and PassMark CPU metrics, supported by comprehensive instruction set support including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions. Memory subsystem performance is characterized by uncached read throughput exceeding 565 GB/s and write speeds reaching 311 GB/s. High data ingestion and retrieval capability is underscored by achieving over 246 million Redis SET operations per second alongside top-tier Clang software compilation throughput. While single-thread decompression and baseline text generation display average scaling, raw prompt processing and computational transformations register within the top tier of cloud instances.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, r7a.32xlarge delivers dense hardware consolidation by packing 1 TB of DDR5 memory and 128 physical cores into a single virtualized host. The dedicated physical core allocation provides predictable multi-tenant isolation and avoids thread contention common in standard simultaneous multithreading profiles. However, the complete reliance on network-attached storage presents an architectural consideration, requiring optimized EBS volume configurations to prevent I/O bottlenecks in disk-heavy environments. This instance is best aligned with large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA or Redis, massive distributed data processing grids, continuous integration pipelines, and memory-bound scientific simulations.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 128 dedicated physical x86_64 cores operating at up to 3.7 GHz with a 1:1 vCPU-to-core mapping. It features 1024 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, providing 8 GB of RAM per core, along with 50 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The instance includes no local storage or discrete GPU hardware, necessitating external storage volumes for stateful persistence. In synthetic and practical benchmarks, the r7a.32xlarge achieves top-tier results in multi-core CPU testing, uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 565 GB/s, and over 246 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance is suited for enterprise-grade in-memory databases, large Redis or Memcached clusters, heavy data warehousing ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency scientific simulations requiring substantial memory capacity.
